question: Should the bundled `onepassword` plugin be allowed to resolve OpenClaw SecretRefs by passing its service-account token to a locally installed, path-validated `op` CLI, including the new `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency?
rationale: This is a new bundled credential-provider and external-executable trust boundary; automated review cannot choose the repository's permanent security and packaging policy.

options.title: Authorize with proof
options.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and bundled CLI trust model after the contributor posts redacted current-head evidence for the real service-account and Gateway path.

options.title: Keep manual exec wiring
options.body: Decline the managed provider surface and retain the documented generic exec-provider configuration for operators who use 1Password.

options.title: Externalize the integration
options.body: Require this provider to ship as an external plugin if maintainers do not want the bundled package to own the token-to-CLI boundary.

recommendation.title: Authorize with proof
recommendation.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and bundled CLI trust model after the contributor posts redacted current-head evidence for the real service-account and Gateway path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the closest merged bundled SecretRef-provider precedent and can provide the intended ownership and operational proof context.
